messages:
zheng: Heads up — after the kernel selector change this morning we're seeing a noticeable spike in soft-429s on prefetch-heavy traffic. p95 soft-429 rate ~3.1% during the 1h window. Anyone else seeing this?

maria: saw the same in us-west2. Quick profile: more small batches being created when prefetch misses happen, plus a few kernel fallbacks. Adds serialization overhead + kernel warmup.

sam: +1. I ran a quick canary adjusting token_budget_target and saw soft-429s drop. Suspect the batcher is shrinking the window when prefetch latency increases, which then cascades.

zheng: can you share the config you used in the canary?

sam: pasted the minimal admit config I tested — lowered soft pressure by increasing token budget and adding a tiny backoff:```
admission:
  token_budget_target: 256
  max_batch_wait_ms: 8
  prefetch_aware: true
  soft_429:
    enabled: true
    backoff_ms: 200
    threshold_pct: 2.0
```

maria: FYI kernel-selector logs show fallback to generic kernel for seq_len 1-8 on the new selector in ~0.6ms extra per token case. That plus smaller batches explains the perf hit. We can either adjust kernel hints or prevent batcher from shrinking so aggressively on prefetch miss.

runtime-oncall: rolling canary policy: start 10% traffic canary in us-west2. If soft-429 > 2.0% after 30m revert. @infra-bot can you tag the canary deployment?

infra-bot: deploy: canary rollout started by @sam — build b-2024.6.13-142. target=us-west2 shard=10%

zheng: good. Additional idea: make admission prefer KV-hit requests inside the admit window (small weight bump) so cold requests don't cause a cascade of small batches. Also consider reserving a tiny token pool for cold-starts to absorb prefetch misses.

maria: prototype reserve looks like: reserve_tokens: 512 at batcher-level. Also watching this Prom query: `sum(rate(runtime_soft_429_total[5m])) by (shard)` — current canary pre-run baseline: `us-west2=0.9, us-east1=0.3` (per 5m).

sam: I'll run 3h canary with the admit config above + reserve_tokens and post back numbers. If it holds we can push admit heuristic change and a minor kernel-selector hint update.

zheng: thanks. If we still see >2% after 30m we rollback and file follow-up perf ticket. For tracking: create perf/regress board card with traces attached.

maria: noted, will add traces and kernel logs to the ticket.

sam: starting canary now.
